וחד אמר (38b.3) -- the other of Rav Dimi and Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda
חזקיה משמיה דאביי (38b.3-4) -- the later amora quoting Abaye, not R' Chiyya's son

props.gloss_en: Beit Hillel: one may even return [a pot to the stove]
according to the one who says 'one returns', one returns even on Shabbat
once we stood before R' Chiyya Rabba; we brought him up a kettle of hot water from the lower storey to the upper, poured him a cup, and returned it to its place
and he [R' Chiyya Rabba] said nothing to us
they taught [that one may return] only while they are still in his hand
but if he put them down on the ground, [returning them] is forbidden
R' Ami: what R' Tadai did, he did for himself
even if he put it down on the ground, [returning it] is permitted
[if] they are still in his hand, [returning them] is permitted
'in hand permitted' was said only when he intends to return it; if he does not intend to return it, it is forbidden
by implication: on the ground, even if he intends to return it, it is forbidden
'on the ground forbidden' was said only when he does not intend to return it; if he intends to return it, it is permitted
by implication: while still in his hand, even if he does not intend to return it, it is permitted

supports.gloss_en: ואף רבי אושעיא סבר אף מחזירין אפילו בשבת, דאמר רבי אושעיא... והחזרנוהו למקומו ולא אמר לנו דבר -- R' Oshaya's report that R' Chiyya Rabba said nothing when the kettle was returned to its place is the stam's evidence that R' Oshaya too holds Rav Sheshet's view
מכלל דעל גבי קרקע אף על פי שדעתו להחזיר אסור -- if even in hand intent is required, on the ground intent does not suffice
מכלל שבעודן בידו אף על פי שאין דעתו להחזיר מותר -- if intent is what matters only on the ground, in hand it is permitted even without it
